scenes.sub: Impermanent loss (IL) is how much the LP position lags simply holding the same starting tokens when their relative price changes: IL = 2√r ÷ (1 + r) − 1 (r = new price ÷ entry price). It's "impermanent" only if price returns. Withdraw after
scenes.vo: Impermanent loss (impermanent loss) is how much the L.P. position lags simply holding the same starting tokens when their relative price changes: impermanent loss equals 2the square root of r divided by (1 + r) minus 1 (r equals new price divided by entry price). It's "impermanent" only if price returns. Withdraw after the move and it's permanent. Full L.P. P and L equals L.P. value + fees + incentives minus gas, compared to hold value.
scenes.cap: Impermanent loss (IL) is how much the LP position lags simply holding the same starting tokens when their relative price changes: IL = 2√r ÷ (1 + r) − 1 (r = new price ÷ entry price). It's "impermanent" only if price returns. Withdraw after the move and it's permanent. Full LP P&L = LP value + fees + incentives − gas, compared to hold value.

scenes.title: Worked example
scenes.vo: Deposit 1 ETH + 3,000 U.S.D.C. at ETH = $3,000 (total $6,000). ETH rises to $4,000. A master judges the L.P. on the +$58, not the +$1,058. Calculator: the calculator Starting $6,000: +$1,058 (mostly from ETH going up, not from LPing). Holding: +$58, the actual value added by LPing.

scenes.q: ETH doubles. IL on a 50/50 pool?
scenes.vo: Question one. ETH doubles. impermanent loss on a 50 to 50 pool? [[pause 4]] The answer: About minus 5.7% versus holding.
scenes.cap: Question 1. ETH doubles. IL on a 50/50 pool? The answer: About −5.7% vs holding.

scenes.a: When you withdraw while the price ratio is different from entry.
scenes.vo: Question three. When does impermanent loss become permanent? [[pause 4]] The answer: When you withdraw while the price ratio is different from entry.
scenes.cap: Question 3. When does IL become permanent? The answer: When you withdraw while the price ratio is different from entry.
